map.hospital_course_summary: A known diabetic (uncontrolled T2DM, on Ayurvedic therapy only, HbA1c 13.9%) and known thyroid patient presented to the ER on 26/2/26 ~6:14 PM with fever, generalized weakness x3 days and myalgia, found hypotensive (BP 87/50), tachycardic (PR 116), tachypneic, with capillary glucose 443 mg/dL (pages 3, 16, 46, 47). Workup showed marked hyperglycemia (RBS 496), ketonuria, glycosuria and metabolic derangement (severe hyponatremia Na 114-128, hypokalemia K 2.65, hypochloremia, mild metabolic acidosis on ABG) consistent with DKA (pages 27, 28). Inflammatory markers were high (CRP 88.23) with neutrophilic leukocytosis and a positive Widal (S. typhi O 1:160/H 1:80), and CT KUB showed features of bilateral acute pyelonephritis (with incidental hepatomegaly, fatty liver, cholelithiasis, tiny renal calculus, minimal ascites, bilateral pleural effusion with subsegmental consolidation); urine culture however returned no significant bacteriuria (pages 29, 41). She was managed in HDU/SDICU/ICU with IV fluids (NS/RL/DNS titrated to glucose), insulin infusion plus sliding-scale and basal Lantus, IV meropenem, pantoprazole, ondansetron, antipyretics (paracetamol), Happy Nerve Plus, soda bicarbonate, and intermittent tramadol; noradrenaline was kept on standby for BP <90/60 (pages 37-39, 42-45, 64-66). The course featured recurrent fever spikes (up to 102-103 F, one uncertain 105 F read), persistent tachycardia (HR up to 142-149), episodes of chills, transient desaturation to high-80s on room air, and at least one hypotensive episode treated with NS bolus (pages 8, 59, 60, 64, 65, 69). Glucose remained high throughout monitoring (BD 389, etc., p25). Echocardiography showed a structurally normal heart with LVEF 60% and only sinus tachycardia (pages 33, 36, 50). Late in the stay she developed right hip pain with restricted movement, raising ? synovitis; ortho opinion and pelvis/hip x-ray were advised and Ultracet/Etoshine started (pages 22, 48, 57). The Foley catheter was removed 1/3/26. The family declined advised further management; the patient was discharged on request the evening of 2/3/26 (pages 2, 23, 56). The typed discharge summary reframes the principal diagnosis as acute gastroenteritis with dehydration and UTI plus suspected colitis (stool with plenty pus cells/RBCs, USG colitis), which does not align with the DKA/pyelonephritis evidence elsewhere in the chart.
